correctness.rationale: Final file /workspace/repairs/1/RESULT.md. The frozen proof at line 118 incorrectly gives coefficient 2 directly after the first odd spike when t=3 and r≥6. The shifted block contributes 1 there, so the coefficient is 3; it is still strictly between the two coefficients 4 in the sense of a dip in the sequence. The repair gives the exact coefficients and spells out the Gorenstein chart cases. Weights are unordered, so take a≤b. The Gorenstein condition gives positive integral Reid–Tai ages in both weight charts; the repeated unit weights with r≥2 rule out pseudoreflections. With x=Q/a≥y=Q/b, integrality and r>0 give y≥2, x≥3. An age-one element exists at y=2 or x=y=3; when y>2 and x>3, the strict inequalities r>d and r+d>a, with d=b−a, exclude age one as detailed in the repair, including d=0 and weight-one charts. The converse family has x=t+2,y=2, or x=y=3. The Ehrhart floor exponents reduce to ceil(m/2)−floor(m/(t+2)); the even period t+2 adds t/2, the odd period 2(t+2) adds t. In the odd base block the two length-(t+2) ranges abut at degree (t+1)/2, giving spike 4 and interior coefficients 2 elsewhere; the equal case writes m=3j+s. These facts give all the stated products. For odd t≥3 the two spikes and the corrected dip give failure iff there are ≥2 blocks. For even t=2c≥6, one block is unimodal; two have a single central overlap of heights 3,3, and three or more give 3,3,2,3 at c,c+1,c+2,2c. Direct block overlap gives a single rise/plateau/fall for t=1,2,4 and for (r,r). Thus all thresholds are unchanged. The supplied script is finite exact regression (coefficient comparison to r=400, age scan to r=60); no fresh replay or formal certification is claimed.
